description:
DECISION TICKET -- needs the user. `send/2`'s contract accepts raw integers, and
the corpus depends on it.

## Premise verified at main 417c5b0b5

    src/modules/runtime_library/kernel.fz:75-76
      @spec send(pid | integer, t) :: t when t: any
      fn send(pid, msg), do: fz_send(pid, msg)

    runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs:468
      pub extern "C" fn fz_send_ref(process: *mut Process,
                                    receiver_pid_bits: u64,
                                    msg_ref_word: u64) -> u64

Raw bits, no registry. `Process` (process.fz) exposes only `heap_alloc_stats/0`.
No `register`, no `whereis`, no named processes anywhere in runtime/src.

15 fixture files use `send(1, ...)` -- e.g. 00016_spawn_then_receive.fz,
00290_spawn_send_receive.fz (`fn child(), do: send(1, 42)`),
00521_relay_process.fz.

## The gap is NARROWER than the old ticket said

The old ticket implies no `self()`, no registry and no pid-threading exist.
`self()` DOES exist (`extern "C" fn fz_self() :: pid`, kernel.fz:8, exposed at
:72), and pid-threading via closure capture works today:

    fn main() do
      parent = self()
      dbg(parent)                                  => 1
      spawn(fn () -> send(parent, 42) end)
      dbg(receive do x -> x end)                   => 42
    end

A pid renders as a bare integer, which is exactly why `send(1, ...)` works at
all. So a CAPTURING child can already obtain the parent's pid. It is specifically
the ZERO-CAPTURE child, `spawn(&child/0)`, that has no route to the parent's pid
-- that is the real gap.

## The three options, unchanged

(a) Keep integer addressing as documented fz semantics.
(b) Add a registry / named processes and tighten the spec to `pid | name`.
(c) Have spawn supply the parent pid to children.

Elixir's contract is `pid | port | atom` (registered name), never an arbitrary
integer.

Whichever is chosen, the 15 fixtures using `send(1, ...)` are the migration
surface, and the answer determines whether `pid` stays representationally an
integer.

Count drift in the old ticket: 15 fixtures, not ~16.
title: Decide the send/2 addressing contract: raw integer pids work only because a pid renders as an integer
